goal: Add an asyncio hang watchdog to the harness that cancels an invocation silent past hang_timeout_seconds, emits harness.hang_detected, and routes to internal_error, disambiguated from an operator interrupt.

references: src/flywheel/harness.py:1856-1892 -- the _on_message closure + invoker(request) call in _drive_iterations; the watchdog resets last_activity from _on_message and races the invocation
src/flywheel/harness.py:1541-1574 -- crash path (running -> internal_error, Outcome.INTERNAL_ERROR); the hang routes to this same class/state
src/flywheel/harness.py:1461-1477 -- _run_attempt's CancelledError handler routing to _handle_interrupt; this is the FR-4 disambiguation point
src/flywheel/harness.py:568-642 -- _handle_interrupt (operator path, harness.interrupted); a watchdog cancel must NOT reach this
constraints: Read the threshold from config.loop_guard.hang_timeout_seconds; when None (the default) the watchdog never starts and behavior is exactly as today.

FR-3: launch invoker(request) as an asyncio.Task alongside a watchdog coroutine that loops on a short sleep comparing mclock() to a last_activity slot updated by the existing _on_message seam (reuse it -- no second subscription). On mclock() - last_activity > hang_timeout_seconds, set a hang_tripped flag, cancel the invocation task, emit harness.hang_detected, finalize with Outcome.INTERNAL_ERROR, and transition running -> internal_error. On normal completion cancel the watchdog cleanly.
Any SDK message -- including a RateLimitEvent or a ThinkingBlock-bearing AssistantMessage -- resets last_activity via _on_message (rate-limit counts as liveness).

FR-4: a watchdog-induced CancelledError routes to the FR-3 internal_error path, NEVER to _handle_interrupt; gate on the hang_tripped flag. An operator interrupt with the watchdog disabled is unchanged from today.
If the invocation result is already produced when the cancel races in, honor it -- check hang_tripped only when the await actually raised CancelledError; no double-finalize.

Add harness tests covering: a stalled message stream past the threshold -> internal_error with exactly one harness.hang_detected and NO harness.interrupted; a heartbeat message just under the threshold each tick -> normal completion, watchdog never trips; a steady RateLimitEvent stream -> never trips; an operator cancel with the watchdog disabled -> unchanged interrupted behavior.
FR-7: assert harness.hang_detected round-trips through flywheel.audit.stream(run_id) under the run's monotonic sequence.
Drive watchdog tests with a controllable monotonic clock (mclock) and a message stream seam rather than real wall-clock sleeps, so tests are deterministic and fast.
Call mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on src/flywheel/harness.py and any touched test file and fix all type errors before verify.
Commit with a Conventional Commits message before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: No grounded default for hang_timeout_seconds -- it ships disabled (None).
No RateLimitInfo.ResetsAt ETA computation -- a rate-limit event is treated only as liveness.
No changes to flywheel.invoker -- on_message and tool_interactions already exist.
edge_cases: The watchdog tick must be coarse enough to add no measurable overhead when disabled (early return before any task/coroutine is created).
A near-simultaneous normal completion and watchdog fire must finalize exactly once.

graders.run: uv run pytest tests/test_harness.py -k "hang or watchdog or interrupt"
graders.name: watchdog-tests
